mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP indicates a growing economy, which leads to higher consumer spending and increased demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive when the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5% indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive when the unemployment rate exceeds 5% (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts and a decrease in the unemployment rate indicate a strong economy with growing demand for goods and services, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative when housing starts increase and unemployment rate decreases (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates an increase in the supply of goods and services, leading to higher economic growth and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative during periods of strong industrial production growth (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the money supply indicate an expansionary monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative when the federal funds rate is below 3.5% and the money supply exceeds 700000 (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and ultimately resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when payroll employment exceeds 160000 (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index indicates decreased demand for goods and services, leading to lower economic growth and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive when the consumer price index is below 320 (t-test p < 0.05).
